/-!
# Executable field arithmetic for the two PCP tests

The literal list contains pairs of claimed answer values and sign coordinates.
The certificate list contains pairs of claimed certificate values and point
coordinates. The surrounding verifier supplies their prescribed lengths.
-/

MIPRE.SAT.PcpFieldTests.TestInput: /-- Modulus, circuit value, claimed main certificate, literals, and zero terms. -/
MIPRE.SAT.PcpFieldTests.checksProg: /-- Both raw coefficient-vector equality tests, as one uniform ambient program. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# Effective evaluation of the routed circuit polynomial

The evaluator multiplies the gate-consistency factors, retaining preceding
input-copy values for routing. It works directly on coefficient vectors and
never expands the polynomial into monomials.
-/

MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.circuitBits: /-- The complete circuit polynomial evaluator on coefficient vectors. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.circuitBitsProg: /-- Uniform polynomial-time evaluation of the routed circuit polynomial.
The input contains the modulus, external coordinates, gate coordinates, and gates. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.factorBits: /-- One gate-consistency factor, with its claimed gate value. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.fieldScanProg: /-- The scan is an ambient polynomial-time program even on malformed inputs. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.fieldStep: /-- Append the gate to the routing history and multiply its consistency factor. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.gatePairs: /-- Pair each actual gate with its supplied coordinate; short malformed
coordinate arrays use the empty vector. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# Restricting polynomials to an embedded set of variables

Setting all other variables to zero preserves every individual-degree bound.
This lets circuit polynomials be written with natural-number input and gate
indices, then restricted to the exact finite variable count used by the PCP.
-/

MIPRE.LowDegree.extendZero: /-- Extend values by zero outside an embedded set of coordinates. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# Circuit arithmetization on exactly the input and gate variables

The first `C.inputs` coordinates are the inputs, followed by the `C.size` gate
variables. No new variables are needed for routing repeated input reads.
-/

MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.finiteArith: /-- The routed polynomial restricted to the exact finite coordinate set. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.gatePart: /-- Read the finite assignment's gate part, with false outside the circuit. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.inputPart: /-- Read the finite assignment's input part, with false outside the circuit. -/
MIPRE.SAT.Circuit.wireEmbedding: /-- Embed the exact finite coordinate set into input and gate indices. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# The raw polynomial-time classical PCP verifier

The verifier rejects invalid specifications and malformed field views, constructs
the exact circuit within the supplied view budget, evaluates its polynomial, and
checks both algebraic identities on coefficient vectors. Its correspondence to
typed low-degree proofs is established separately.
-/

MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifierCertifica: /-- Pair the certificate evaluations after the main certificate with each coordinate. -/
MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifierCircuitVa: /-- Evaluate the concrete circuit polynomial at the supplied field point. -/
MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifierFormat: /-- The constructed parameter family's exact raw view check. -/
MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifierLiterals: /-- Pair the five claimed answer evaluations with the five sign coordinates. -/
MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifierModulus: /-- Construct the binary field modulus once from its unary degree. -/
MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifierTests: /-- Both field identities, including the single circuit-polynomial evaluation. -/
MIPRE.TM.CookLevin.Pad.verifyPcp: /-- The actual globally polynomial-time verifier, with both mandatory rejection checks. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# Certificates for polynomials vanishing on the Boolean cube

The paper's `prop:zero-basis`, used in classical PCP completeness. Reduction by
`X i * (1 - X i)` preserves every individual-degree bound. This is stronger than
the total-degree bound in the general combinatorial Nullstellensatz.
-/

MIPRE.LowDegree.cubeZero: /-- The univariate Boolean-cube constraint at coordinate `i`. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# The algebraic tests of the classical PCP

The formula test and Boolean-cube zero test from `thm:pcp-decider`. These lemmas
concern polynomials and their evaluations. Circuit padding, the embedding of the
five answer blocks, and the verifier's ambient program are separate obligations.
-/

MIPRE.SAT.PcpAlgebra.Accepts: /-- The two equalities tested by the algebraic verifier at one point. -/
MIPRE.SAT.PcpAlgebra.constraint: /-- The constraint polynomial: a clause is violated exactly when all five factors
are nonzero on the Boolean cube and its describing formula accepts. -/
MIPRE.SAT.PcpAlgebra.zeroCombination: /-- The polynomial reconstructed from the claimed zero-basis certificates. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# The five disjoint answer blocks of the classical PCP

The answer polynomials have `m` variables; the formula and certificates have
`5*m + 5 + s` variables. This file transports the former into the latter without
losing the individual-degree bound. In particular, the honest constraint has
degree at most seven, rather than the soundness proof's coarse bound of 41.
-/

MIPRE.SAT.PcpAlgebra.TypedAccepts: /-- The two tests on the point and its claimed field-valued evaluations. -/
MIPRE.SAT.PcpAlgebra.liftAnswer: /-- An answer polynomial, viewed as a polynomial on the complete PCP point. -/
MIPRE.SAT.PcpParams.blockIndex: /-- The coordinate of an answer bit within the complete PCP point. -/
MIPRE.SAT.PcpParams.signIndex: /-- The sign coordinates immediately follow the five answer blocks. -/

The describer reads five little-endian indices followed by their signs. This

-/

MIPRE.SAT.cubeIndex: /-- A Boolean cube point as a little-endian index. -/
MIPRE.SAT.indexCube: /-- The Boolean cube point named by a little-endian index. -/

module_doc:
/-!
# Answer reduction, supplied

Piece AR-6 of `planning/answer-reduction.md` (`thm:answer-reduction`): the `AnswerReduction 5`
contract, inhabited by `arVerifier` over the classical PCP decider
(`TM.CookLevin.Pad.classicalPcpDecider`). The three hypotheses the construction and its analysis
ask of the PCP decider hold for it:

* its field is the Shoup field (`shoupField_classical`), by definition;
* its parameters are polynomial in `(log n, log T, Q, σ)` (`exists_paramsBound_classical`): the
  padded dimension is, and the field degree is polylogarithmic in `Q m'`;
* its field is eventually larger than every fixed power of `8 (Q + 1) m'`
  (`fieldLarge_classical`), from the field degree's square term.

The contract's clauses are then `arVerifier_bounds` (the complexity clause and the answer cut
below the output bound), `arVerifier_hasPerfectPCC` (completeness at the cut, hence at the bound)
and `arVerifier_soundness` (at the output bound).
-/

MIPRE.AnswerReduction.arA: /-- The constant `a` of the soundness loss. -/
MIPRE.AnswerReduction.arB: /-- The exponent `b` of the soundness loss. -/
MIPRE.AnswerReduction.classicalR: /-- The parameter polynomial of the classical PCP decider. -/
